title: Review a data model
summary: Find missing constraints and indexes in a proposed relational schema.

scenario.briefing: A proposed schema will hold customers and orders. Review it for identity, relationships, valid ranges, and query performance before it reaches production.

objectives.description: Identify missing keys, constraints, and indexes.

hints: Every table needs a stable primary key.
Totals and dates have valid ranges that constraints can enforce.
Add primary keys, a foreign key, nonnegative total and quantity checks, and an index on orders.customer_id and placed_at.

misconceptions.description: Assuming application code is enough to protect data integrity.
misconceptions.feedback: Applications can have bugs and multiple writers. Database constraints enforce invariants at the shared boundary.

misconceptions.description: Adding indexes without a query workload.
misconceptions.feedback: Indexes cost write time and space. Add them for measured or clearly expected query patterns.

sections.title: Constraints encode invariants
sections.body: A primary key gives a row identity. A foreign key prevents orders from pointing at missing customers. CHECK constraints reject impossible totals and quantities. These rules hold even when another application writes to the database.

sections.title: Indexes serve queries
sections.body: An index speeds lookups on selected columns at the cost of storage and write work. Index columns used for joins, filters, and ordering by frequent queries. Measure before adding broad indexing.

vocabulary.definition: A database rule that rejects invalid data.
A constraint linking a column to another table's key.
A structure that speeds selected lookups.

steps.title: Review the proposed schema
steps.prompt: Select every supported finding and choose a verdict.

artifact.title: Proposed schema
artifact.caption: Intended for the campus storefront.

findings.label: Neither table has a primary key.
orders.customer_id has no foreign key to customers.
total_cents and placed_at have no validity constraints.
The customer and date query has no supporting index.
Customer name is a suitable primary key.

verdicts.label: Reject until keys, foreign key, checks, and the query index are defined
Deploy now and add constraints after launch

steps.explanation: The schema has no identity, relationship, range constraints, or index for its stated query. Names are not stable unique identifiers.

steps.title: Why constraints live in the database

statements.label: Constraints protect data shared by multiple writers.
A primary key gives every row a stable identity.
Foreign keys help prevent orphaned rows.

steps.explanation: Constraints enforce invariants near the data. Indexes trade storage and writes for read speed.

accessibility.summary: The schema and findings are text with standard checkboxes and a radio verdict.
accessibility.keyboardNotes: Use Space for findings and arrow keys for the verdict.
accessibility.screenReaderNotes: The schema is announced as a code block. Findings and verdict feedback are read in order.
